newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish announce EU presidency consumer priorities.
newsitem.headline: Irish announce EU presidency consumer priorities.

text.p: Ireland announced on Tuesday its priorities for consumer policy during its presidency of the European Union, pledging to take further steps to strengthen consumer rights.

Pat Rabbitte, Ireland's minister for commerce, science and technology, said the Irish presidency aimed to advance a draft directive on consumer access to justice, COM(95)712, at the Consumer Council on November 25.

"It is part of the programme for the completion of the Single European Market and recognises the impact of the development and proliferation of new distance selling techniques," Rabbitte said in a statement.
The directive would allow injunctions to be invoked against suppliers in one member state who act unlawfully towards consumers in another member state, he said.
The November Council will also debate a European Commission action plan on the settlement of individual consumer disputes, COM(96)13, Rabbitte said.

"The Commission action plan, when taken in conjunction with the draft directive on access to justice, is designed to provide consumers with an informal and speedy means of redress in relation to complaints," he said.

Rabbitte said agreement would also be sought in November for an amendment to the directive on consumer credit, setting a common formula for the calculation of APR (annualised percentage rates) throughout the EU, COM(96)79.

Finally, Ireland would facilitate debate on a draft directive on guarantees and after sales service, and allow consumer ministers to provide input to recent Commission green papers on financial services and commercial communications, Rabbitte said.
